description:
Measures whether a product's exploitation risk is chronic or a one-off, for patch prioritization.

Does in-the-wild exploitation risk STICK to proven products, or SPREAD to new ones? Analyzes CISA KEV: correlates each product's historical known-exploited count against its RECENT KEV additions (Spearman rho), and splits recent additions into repeat-offenders (products with a prior KEV) vs first-time products.

Answers "how should I prioritize patching — chase the chronic offenders, or watch for newcomers?" The result is computed live: it reports rho, the repeat-offender versus first-time split, the share concentrated in the 20 most-exploited products, and an `interpretation` sentence. This is product-level stickiness, a proxy for exploitation dynamics, not proof of exploit timing.

Public read (no auth). Pass {"days": N} for the recent window (30-720, default 180).
name: kev-exploitation-stickiness
title: KEV exploitation stickiness
